record.title: Bulgaria stages origin-based and third-country pandemic entry prohibitions
record.scope: Admission restrictions at all border checkpoints, including land and rail
record.crossings: Bulgarian land frontiers; regime rather than universal gate closure
record.movement: Initially non-exempt arrivals from named risk origins; subsequently non-exempt third-country entrants and restricted European-origin categories
record.exceptions: Bulgarian citizens, family and qualifying residents; later notices preserve health workers, freight personnel, diplomats, military, humanitarian workers and specified return transit. May permissions broadened further.
record.imposing_authority: Bulgarian Minister of Health; Border Police
record.enforcement: Health minister orders communicated by consulates and Border Police; no claim that every checkpoint was physically sealed.
record.consequences: Ordinary inbound passenger travel restricted; freight personnel among exceptions.
record.relationship: Separate from Turkish reciprocal restrictions and Bulgarian nationalist blockades R2-EU-012/013. Initial and broadened COVID phases retained as one mixed regime.
record.status_observation: Historical evidence only; no status inference at 21 October 2026
record.official_rationale: Limit the spread of COVID-19 from affected countries.
record.context: An initial risk-origin prohibition was widened to third-country nationals from 20 March; EU/Schengen admission was formally restored in May while other restrictions continued.
record.uncertainty: 18 March is the legal start of the initial origin-based phase. 22 May is formal partial easing, not full third-country reopening. The intermediate order sequence and actual first passages are not fully reconstructed.

historical.duration_note: Formal change of permission; operational reopening and continuous effective duration not established. No operational duration: affected categories changed, and the endpoint is formal partial easing.
